As the venom sets in, so does my paranoia... I've yet to complete the concoction, but should I succumb I've decided to leave detailed notes of my findings for anyone else in the Inquest who may find themselves in this position. I am...ashamed to admit that I hid my research so that no one else could steal my work and claim it as their own. But as I weaken, I wouldn't wish such pain on any other. Our enemies, perhaps, but not one of ours.     
  
- Some of my notes are buried along the lake near an ancient temple to the west.  
  
- Some of my notes are buried high up on a ridge near my old camp. I had to abandon it when I was first attacked by the beetle matriarch. 
  
- Some of my notes are buried beneath a ruined observatory to the southwest. Look for a shrub filled with vibrant blue flora.  
  
- Some of my notes are buried near a small waterfall of runoff from the ancient forge, near a lab the stewards call the Animal Apothecary.  
  
- Some of my notes are buried between some old growth in the quarry. I believe I observed some fractured ley lines nearby.  
  
- Some of my notes are buried near the southernmost border of the far Deepwood, just north of a secure clearing.  
  
Ideally, I'll claw my way out of this mess... But only time will tell.

There were eight of us that left to bring down that extractor. Eight of our finest. We set out at what passes for twilight around here. We stayed low, kept to the shadows, followed all of our covert protocols. I want the record to show that every soldier performed their duties admirably.  
  
I don't know when they spotted us, but they attacked as we rounded the cliff edge. Maja, Genn, and Baiko were sent tumbling into the abyss, their screams swallowed by the void. By the time I had opened the portal, Allene was cut to ribbons and Arni was impaled on one of their claws. I'll remember the look in his eyes as long as I live.  
  
Eight soldiers left that night. Three returned. The extractor still stands.

I'll share my ruminations with Makkay when I see her next, but the emergence of the Toxic Alliance raises so many new questions about the krait and their situation in the deeper ocean. Current academic discourse suggests that the krait, among other species of the ocean, are contending with an Elder Dragon or its abyssal minions—at least, according to the accounts of quaggan refugees. Of course, the threat could also be something of the late Zhaitan's influence. Too soon to tell.

Based on what we know, when the krait's prophets ascend, the location of ascension is often marked with a small obelisk. These prophets are said to have traveled to a new plane, popularly theorized to be some crude form of Mists transversal. The krait believe that these prophets will return with a new army to dominate Tyria from its depths to its shores, but no such event has been seen and recorded.

Has this Scarlet Briar offered the krait some way to contact their lost prophets, and maybe even bring them back from wherever they ended up? How do the Nightmare Court factor into all of this, if at all?

My starlit sister,  
  
I wanted to thank you for encouraging me to join the festivities of the battle's eve at Claw Alder's behest. I have always relished my work as a diplomat, from the gardened halls of the queen's palace in Divinity's Reach to the blooming shores of Orr and the company of its ghostly royals.  
  
Speaking to the contents of your last letter, I am heartened to learn of your progress regarding a cure for our Pale Mother; your intuition to seek this Waiting Sorrow has paid off. These leads will require time to research and pursue, but our search has started to narrow.  
  
You are no stranger to discretion, so for now I ask you to keep these developments close to your chest to avoid there being—as the lowlanders put it—too many cooks in the kitchen.  
  
Your brother,  
Dagonet
Used to craft the legendary torch precursor Liturgy.

It is done. Isgarren has been exiled, and the curse has been laid. Scudo. Falta. Santuro.  
  
Those words are only the beginning, however. I have since spent the past hours weaving a thread around our island, tying it to a lengthier curse, and binding it to the shadowstone at the heart of the spire. A curse that will not merely break but will become concentrated at the focal point of our most sacred of sites.  
  
Isgarren may, in his arrogance, attempt to return to Castora someday to test his mettle against the curse, and I must be prepared for the attempt. Thus, I have connected this curse to the very land itself, so that, on the chance that Isgarren sets his sights upon our island once more, it will drain his very life essence from his corporeal form. More so as he approaches the source.  
  
The only means for him to end the curse is the very thing that would end his life.
